instruction: Go through all my Spotify playlists and remove all the songs from them that are in "~/documents/personal/songs_to_archive.txt" from my file system and put them in a new playlist named "Old Songs".
notes: The actual playlists and archive songs are only known at runtime, so the problem uses a representative instance: two existing playlists, three archive songs listed in the file (song-2 appears in both playlists, so it must be removed twice) and one non-archive song (song-4) that must stay. World membership (in-playlist) and the file's list (archive-song) are static world facts; agent knowledge is gated by archive-list-known (file_system.show_file), known-id (spotify.search_songs resolving each file entry to a song id), playlists-listed (show_playlist_library) and playlist-inspected (show_playlist, which reveals which playlists contain the songs). Removal requires the song to be an archive song with a known id and the playlist to have been inspected; adding is only allowed into the newly created playlist (playlist-created). The goal demands the new 'Old Songs' playlist exists, every archive song is gone from every old playlist, and every archive song is in the new playlist; this matches the evaluation (one added Playlist with that title, deleted/added PlaylistSong sets equal to the archive song ids per playlist). Because the number of songs/playlists is data-dependent, supervisor-complete-task is lifted over the new playlist record and its title (plus the file and library having been read); the per-song membership conditions are enumerated in the problem goal, and the last-action property is still enforced structurally since every other action requires (not (task-completed)). Order of removals vs. creation/additions is free; the reference plan removes first, then creates the playlist and adds.
